newsitem.title: USA: Latam banking woes not unique to region - BIS exec.
newsitem.headline: Latam banking woes not unique to region - BIS exec.

text.p: The financial woes faced by Latin America's banks are not unique to the region and should not be treated as such by regulators, said Andrew Crockett, general manager at the Bank for International Settlements.

"Latin America has not been alone in facing financial difficulties and fragility and the sources of the problems are not unique," said Crockett, speaking to an audience of bankers and regulators at the Inter-American Development Bank here.
He cited an IMF study which found that 131 of 181 member countries had suffered significant banking crises in the past.

He also noted that macroeconomic volatility or fluctuating interest rates -- a major source of concern for Latin America's banking system -- were at the root of banking problems in the Spanish and Nordic banking systems as well as the Savings and Loan crisis in the U.S.
"That means that the rules and practices that have to be adopted in Latin America ... have to be consistent with those being adopted in other countries facing similar problems," Crockett added.

"We need to have an overall comprehensive umbrella of banking standards, practices and understandings that is applicable in any area of the world, depending upon the particular circumstances of the individual countries," Crockett said.
He said such an "umbrella" did not preclude national differentiation where internationally agreed upon standards were insufficient.
He added however, that it would be "very unfortunate" to design rules that were "generically different in different areas of the world."
